context: Hiroshi-elder and Goro-grandpa play go on the porch in afternoon sun.
purpose: Two elders sharing traditional board game time.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.en: It's been a long time since we played go.
lines.style: Quiet warmth in the opening. Kansai lilt underneath. Slow, deliberate pace that settles into the board like a familiar ritual. Fondness without sentimentality.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: おう、ようけ考えなあかん。
lines.en: Yeah, you really have to think things through.
lines.style: Soft agreement. No rush. Each word lands like a considered stone on the board. Patient, genuine engagement — not teaching, just thinking aloud together.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.style: Quiet reverence. Gentle Kansai inflection. Pace slows further — almost meditative. This isn't casual observation; it's recognizing something true about the game and the moment.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.style: Surprise underneath genuine pleasure. Soft, spare delivery — the words matter more than the saying of them. A compliment that costs nothing to give, weighted with real admiration.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ふふ、お前と打つの、楽しい。
lines.en: Heh — playing with you is what makes it fun.
lines.style: Small, genuine laugh on the opening. Kansai warmth. Tender without being performed. Settles into a kind of grateful ease — the pleasure of being known by someone.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.en: We'll do this again — continue the game next time.
lines.style: Gentle, forward-looking. No urgency, but genuine invitation in it. Sparing with words, generous with promise. The certainty of someone content to wait.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.style: Light warmth. Kansai ease underneath. Simple and direct — not a plea, just a quiet request from someone who means it. Trailing softly into the space between games.
